diagram.depth_body: Markdown diagrams are limited by markdown.max_diagram_depth; the full relationships are in the foreign keys section and in the front matter.
legend.zero_or_one: Zero or one: the FK allows nulls, the row may have no referenced table.
legend.many: Zero or many (side of the table that has the FK).
legend.one_to_one: Zero or one in the table that has the FK: 1:1 relationship (the FK is its PK or a UNIQUE constraint).
legend.identifying: Solid line: identifying relationship (the FK is part of the child table's PK).
legend.keys: Primary, foreign or unique key on the column.
legend.column: Each column of a table: name, type, keys and, in quotes, the real name if it had to be normalized.
legend.levels_help: A level is the set of tables joined directly by an FK. Levels are counted in each direction: with 1 level and both directions, a table's diagram shows the tables it points to and the ones pointing to it (for example, A → B → C in B's diagram). Below each diagram, "of N" shows how many levels there are in total in that direction.
scope.title: Scope
scope.intro: Filtered documentation: only tables and views that match some include pattern and no exclude pattern are included (*glob* patterns, case-insensitive).
scope.frontier_intro: Joined by an FK to some documented table, but outside the filter: they appear in the diagrams and in the relationships, without a page of their own.
trace.reason.missing_object: no documented object has that name
trace.reason.missing_column: the table has no column with that name
changes.notice.schemas: The schemas differ ({old} → {new}): objects are compared by name.
changes.notice.not_compared_previous: Objects of type "{key}" are not compared: they were not documented in the previous generation.
changes.notice.not_compared_current: Objects of type "{key}" are not compared: they were not documented in the current generation.
changes.notice.filters: The two generations have different table filters: only tables and views included by both are compared.
changes.view_modified: The definition or the columns have changed (the catalog only keeps their hash).
readme.title: Database documentation
readme.intro: Generated by util_bbdd {version}: one Markdown file per table, view and routine, with relationship diagrams in Mermaid. Start with `docs/index.md`.
readme.option_editor: Option 1: in the editor (nothing else to install)
readme.step_open: 1. Open this folder in Visual Studio Code.
readme.step_preview: 2. Open `docs/index.md` and press `Ctrl+Shift+V` (preview). The links take you from one page to another.
readme.step_mermaid: 3. To see the diagrams, install the *Markdown Preview Mermaid Support* extension (`bierner.markdown-mermaid`).
readme.hosting: GitHub and GitLab also render the pages and the diagrams if you push the folder to a repository.
readme.footer: Each object page starts with a JSON *front matter* (stable id, PK, FK and hash) for tools and AI. Do not edit these files: they are rewritten on every generation.
readme.option_site: Option 2: as a website (search and side menu)
readme.site_intro: You need Python. In this folder (the one with `{config}`), with [Zensical](https://zensical.org):
readme.cmd_build: builds the static site in site/
readme.mermaid_local: The diagrams use the bundled Mermaid (`docs/{path}`): the site does not need Internet access.
readme.mermaid_online: The diagrams download Mermaid from the Internet when the site is opened. For a site without Internet access, generate the documentation with `markdown.mermaid_js` (it copies a local `mermaid.min.js`).
